Geography for the smartboard

116 playable adaptations of your 58-topic plan. Search 7A, 7BC or a topic in the Geography library. There are 29 activities in each player mode.

Run a lesson

  1. Choose Geography, the grade and player mode. Open a game.
  2. Review its practice source. Edit prompts and answers; map challenges also accept uploaded maps and editable markers.
  3. Teams choose 2–6 names at launch. Each team submits before the shared answer review. Two-player games give each student an independent touch panel and a shared completion goal.
  4. Complete recognition, application and explanation checkpoints. Correct tasks earn 100 points. Written or spoken explanations are checked by a teacher or partner against a model.
  5. Finish with an individual response on paper or aloud using the learning-check prompt. No student responses are stored.

What has been adapted

These are board-based adaptations using nine challenge types, rather than 116 separate simulation engines. Physical construction, hidden photographs, interviews, charades and longer writing tasks become schematic maps, practice evidence, interactive controls and teacher-reviewed explanations. The original description and the implemented task appear below.

All numerical datasets and project budgets are labelled classroom examples. Schematic maps are for location reasoning, not navigation or exact measurement. Scale tasks state their own units. Uploaded maps should match the teacher’s marker positions and answer key.

The supplied attachment did not contain the textbook pages, photographs, climate graphs or the linked spreadsheet’s individual learning checks. The Thames case file therefore uses an explicitly fictional practice event, not invented facts about the assigned case study. Africa’s history uses source-evaluation practice rather than a claimed reconstruction of unseen chapter events. Replace these sources with your assigned materials before assessing textbook recall. The river-landform starter set names its six features so you can adjust it to your chapter.

Partner panels are public on the shared board. Tasks do not pretend to keep a photograph or source secret from the other player. Students compare their reasoning and both complete the expedition.

Task controls

  • Source detective: read evidence and choose a supported answer
  • Sequence builder: tap shuffled stages into order
  • Map mission: locate the correct lettered marker
  • Scale builder: adjust a visible measurement
  • Memory map: study, hide and recall
  • Landscape profiles: compare drawn cross-sections
  • Glacier lab: vary accumulation and melting, then test mass balance
  • Planning challenge: select projects within a token budget
  • Evidence defence: explain aloud or on paper, then review against a model

Tap controls work with touch or keyboard. No countdown is required. Use Full screen on the smartboard. Save to My lessons on this browser, or download a lesson file including uploaded maps for another device.
